clauses.requirement: Where a lamp (function) uses incandescent technology only, it shall be deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time (Table A8-1 timing, per Annex 8 para 2.1), if the luminous intensity values measured according to paragraph 1.1 are compliant.

Where a lamp (function) uses LED technology only, it shall be deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time (Table A8-1 timing, per Annex 8 para 2.1), if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2 are compliant.

Where a lamp (function) uses any other light generating technology, its corresponding intensity requirements shall be tested and checked for compliance at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.

Where a lamp (function) uses more than one light generating technology, its corresponding intensity requirements shall be tested following the strictest time requirements of paragraphs 2.1.1 to 2.1.3 for the combination of technologies and checked for compliance.

In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the corresponding minimum intensity requirements of a lamp (function) shall be tested and checked for compliance at all points in time, starting at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.

The rear retro-reflector (retro-reflector for motor vehicles, independent or combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight) shall be approved according to the applicable series of amendments of UN R150 (00 or 01) as per Table 2 and its change index (0 or 1); a dash in Table 2 means the device is not available for type approval under that series of amendments.
The retro-reflector shall carry the approval marking and other markings as specified in the administrative provisions of UN R150 paragraph 3.3.
The retro-reflector shall comply with the general provisions on approval marking and other markings of UN R150 paragraph 3.3.1.
